goals: Mechanistic: quantify how water partitioning (ET vs surface runoff vs sub-surface drainage/recharge) and snowpack differ between a wet year (1993) and a dry year (2002) across the basin's elevation gradient
Validation: check basin water balance / runoff against in-domain USGS stream gauges (limited — see feasibility)
key_processes: precipitation partitioning into ET, surface runoff, sub-surface drainage
snow accumulation and melt timing (SWE) at higher elevations
antecedent soil-moisture and storage control on interannual runoff

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM resolves the full water/energy partitioning and snow at each point; the wet/dry contrast is a forcing-period swap, exactly the lever the stack pulls best. NLDAS-2 gives elevation-varying precip so an elevation gradient is meaningful.

answerable: Interannual (wet vs dry) contrast in ET / surface runoff / sub-surface drainage at each column
Elevation dependence of that contrast via NLDAS-2 orographic precip and simulated snow/SWE (resolved to ~12 km)
Soil-texture control on partitioning within each elevation band

not_answerable.aspect: Quantitative validation against USGS stream-gauge hydrographs
not_answerable.why: Single-column ELM has no lateral transport or routing, so it cannot produce integrated streamflow at a gauge
12 km NLDAS cells average over sub-grid terrain; no within-cell lapse rate

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation band x dominant soil), same columns run under two forcing years
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 elevation bands capture the rain->rain-snow->snowmelt gradient that dictates how a wet/dry anomaly redistributes; 2 soil classes per band separate texture control from elevation. Each of the 6 columns is run for BOTH 1993 and 2002 (12 column-years), so the wet/dry contrast is within-column and needs no extra columns.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Distribute across the 2400 m relief with emphasis on the mid-elevation rain-snow transition, where interannual differences in snow fraction most strongly reprogram partitioning; anchor low-band points nearer valley/mainstem and high-band points on upper headwater terrain.
sampling_strategy.replication: No blind replication; the 2 soil classes per band act as the light replication and isolate texture vs elevation.

sampling_plan.reason: Rain/ET-dominated valley point on sandier soil; isolates how a dry year suppresses ET and runoff where snow is negligible.
Same low band on finer soil; separates texture effect on runoff/drainage from elevation at the warm end of the gradient.
Rain-snow transition on coarse soil; captures the band most sensitive to wet/dry snow-fraction shifts.
Rain-snow transition on fine soil; tests whether soil texture modulates snowmelt partitioning in the transition zone.
Snowmelt-dominated headwater on coarse soil; isolates how wet vs dry snowpack drives melt-season drainage/recharge.
Snowmelt-dominated headwater on fine soil; contrasts retention vs drainage under the two snow years.

validation_design.target_variable: basin runoff (surface + sub-surface, wet vs dry)
validation_design.comparison: aggregated — column runoff (QOVER+QDRAI) summed/area-weighted across columns compared qualitatively to gauge annual runoff for 1993 vs 2002; NOT a co-located hydrograph match (no routing)
validation_design.metric: sign and relative magnitude of wet-minus-dry runoff anomaly; annual runoff ratio
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on number of active gauges in HUC 15060103

validation_design.comparison: analog — SNOTEL is sparse/missing in-domain; if any nearby station exists it can only serve as an analog process check, not co-located validation

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 forcing, native SSURGO soil, WTD-informed warm start + spin-up, each column run for wet year 1993 and dry year 2002

requires_capabilities.why: USGS gauges measure integrated streamflow that independent 1-D columns cannot produce
12 km NLDAS cells average over the 2400 m relief
high-elevation partitioning hinges on snow but no in-domain SWE obs are listed
requires_capabilities.blocks: snow validation at the elevations that matter most

requires_capabilities.capability: WTD-informed warm start + multi-year spin-up execution
requires_capabilities.why: interannual drainage/recharge depends on antecedent storage; cold start biases slow states
requires_capabilities.blocks: trustworthy sub-surface partitioning differences between years

assumptions: 1993 is representative of a regional wet year and 2002 of a dry year for this basin within the 1980-2018 NLDAS record
Native SSURGO profiles fall into a coarse and a fine class per band; exact soil values assigned downstream
Concrete column coordinates and their true elevations are assigned by the downstream DEM/soil sampler within the bbox and stated elevation bands
open_questions: How many active USGS gauges lie in HUC 15060103, and do their records cover both 1993 and 2002?
Should the wet/dry years be confirmed against a basin PRISM/NLDAS precip anomaly before committing to 1993/2002?
Is any SNOTEL station close enough to serve even as an analog snow check?
